eyebrow: Lesson 21 · B1 · Good Table Manners · 20 câu
heading: Welcome to the Table
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Table Manners – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 4–7.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Table Manners (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: When guests come to your house, {greet|greet} them at the door. Take their coats and hang them up on {hangers|hangers}; don't throw them in a big pile on the floor.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Shake hands with your guests and hug your relatives, even Aunt Edna with her bad breath and {false teeth|false teeth}! A warm welcome makes everyone feel at home from the very first minute.

paras.label: C
paras.text: At the dinner table, {be a pal|be a pal}. Pull out a chair for a lady or an older guest and hold it {steady|steady} while she sits down and moves closer to the table.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Then find your own seat and sit up straight. Put your napkin on your {lap|lap}, and keep your elbows off the table. You don't want to look like a {barbarian|barbarian} at a {feast|feast}!

paras.label: E
paras.text: Rules about hands are different around the world. In France, for example, it is considered rude to keep your hands under the table. Both hands should stay {visible|visible}, resting near your plate, for the whole meal.

vocab.vi: tử tế như một người bạn
người man rợ, thiếu văn minh

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp cho mỗi đoạn. Mỗi tiêu đề dùng một lần.
options: How to sit at the table

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A: chào khách ở cửa, treo áo khoác.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B: bắt tay, ôm họ hàng.

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C: kéo ghế, giữ ghế cho khách ngồi.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D: ngồi thẳng, khăn ăn trên đùi, không chống khuỷu tay.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: phong tục ở Pháp.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: What should you do with your guests' coats?
The writer suggests hugging your relatives only if you like them.
questions.why: Sai. *even Aunt Edna with her bad breath and false teeth!*

questions.q: Why does the writer mention Aunt Edna's bad breath?
options: to show that you should be welcoming even when it isn't easy
to give advice about cleaning your teeth
to explain why some relatives stay at home
to describe what she had for lunch
questions.why: Dù không dễ chịu vẫn nên đón tiếp nồng hậu.

questions.q: According to (C), how can you help someone sit down?
options: Pull out their chair and hold it steady.
Show them where the bathroom is.
questions.why: *Pull out a chair… and hold it steady.*

questions.q: The writer says it is fine to rest your elbows on the table.
questions.why: Sai. *keep your elbows off the table.*

questions.q: In France, where should your hands be during a meal?
questions.why: *Both hands should stay visible, resting near your plate.*

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Who is the elderly woman most likely to be?
questions.alt: A smiling girl holds up a coat beside a pile of clothes and says: Hi Aunt Edna! to an elderly woman with glasses

questions.q: According to (A), what should the girl do with the coats?
options: Leave them in a pile on the floor.
questions.why: *don't throw them in a big pile on the floor.*
questions.alt: A smiling girl holds up a coat beside a pile of clothes and says: Hi Aunt Edna! to an elderly woman with glasses

questions.q: Which rule is the boy breaking?
options: Keep your elbows off the table.
questions.why: Đoạn D: *keep your elbows off the table.*
questions.alt: A bored-looking boy sits at a dining table with his elbow on the table and his chin in his hand, while a dog lies under his chair

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: Last Sunday, we had a big dinner for Grandad's birthday. [1] When everyone came to the table, I pulled out Grandma's chair for her. [2] During the meal, I sat up straight with my napkin on my lap. [3]
options: I stood at the front door to welcome the guests and hang up their coats.
Then I put my elbows on the table and fell asleep.
She smiled and said I was a real gentleman.
Nobody came because Grandad had forgotten to invite them.
At the end, Grandad said my table manners were better than his!

items.why: Khách đến → chào và treo áo.
Phản ứng của bà khi được kéo ghế.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *At the dinner table, be a pal* (C). To **be a pal** means to…
questions.why: **Pal** = bạn → cư xử tử tế, giúp đỡ.

questions.q: *…look like a barbarian at a feast!* (D). A **barbarian** is someone who…
options: is wild and has no manners
